newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: NEW SLOVAK FORFAITING-FACTORING FIRM LAUNCHED.
newsitem.headline: NEW SLOVAK FORFAITING-FACTORING FIRM LAUNCHED.

text.p: Czech Transfinance a.s. Praha and the Slovak investestment firm Agroinvest on Tuesday launched a joint Slovak-based forfaiting and factoring unit, Transfinance Slovakia a.s..

"In the initial stage, the new firm will specialise only in export activities of Slovak producers, with potential expansion to covering Slovak import contracts," Peter Lukac, head of Transfinance Slovakia told a news conference on Tuesday.
The firm, in which both partners hold a 50 percent stake, expects an anunal turnover of around 100 million crowns, but said that should rise to some 500 million crowns per year within three years.
It began with basic capital of two million Slovak crowns.
Overall volumes of forfaiting and factoring transactions in Slovakia totalled some 2.5 billion crowns last year.

Transfinance a.s. Praha is 30 percent owned by Hypo-Bank AG Munich, (30 percent), Intermarket Factoring AG Vienna (25 percent), Factorfrance Heller S.A. Paris (25 percent) and Czech Zivnobanka (20 percent) .
Its last year turnover totalled around 6.5 billion Czech crowns last year, about half of the Czech factoring and forfaiting market estimated at some 12 to 13 billion crowns.
Agroinvest a.s. Bratislava is a 100-percent doughter company of Slovakia's fourth largest commercial bank Polnobanka a.s.

Lukac said Transfinance Slovakia would cooperate with all major world factoring and forfaiting companies through the owners of its Czech sister firm, but that small basic capital will not allow it to be directly included in world chains, such as Factors Chain International. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
